Commentary: H Crocombe to Jack Edwards, 1 run, on a length around middle and leg, Jack Edwards nudges it towards wide long-on for a single. 11 runs needed from 7 balls

Brook is having a lengthy discussion with the bowler before the final ball of this over, they're making a few changes in the field. Now, Overton joins the discussion. And the Australian spectators seem unhappy with the delay, a lot of boos in the crowd
H Crocombe to Ben Dwarshuis, no run, ends the over with a slower one outside off, Ben Dwarshuis swings and misses. Crocombe wears a cheeky smile
Sam Curran [3.0-0-23-1] is back into the attack
Australia need 11 runs from 6 balls. Are we in for a Super over tonight? We shall find out soon. Curran to bowl the 20th over as he makes the required field changes and starts steaming in to bowl

Sam Curran to Jack Edwards, SIX, Jack Edwards - as cool as a cucumber. A loose delivery by Sam Curran. Back of a length delivery on leg, and it has been swiped over deep backward square leg with disdain. Made it look so effortless did Edwards. Equation down to 5 off 5, and Curran makes a few changes in the field once again

Sam Curran to Jack Edwards, 2 runs, excellent running between the wickets. On a length around middle and leg, Jack Edwards drags it towards wide long-on, and calls for two straightaway. The throw comes in at the keeper's end who whips off the bails, but the batsman slides his bat and makes it
Sam Curran to Jack Edwards, no run, on the shorter side outside off, tad slow, Jack Edwards goes for a pull, but gets beaten due to the lack of pace
Australia need 3 runs in 3 balls - a cracking finish on the cards. A lot of boos in the stands as Curran is making the batsman wait. Testing his patience

Sam Curran to Jack Edwards, 2 runs, scores level. Sam Curran goes full and Jack Edwards drills this right past the bowler. And by the time the fielder cuts it down and releases the ball, they manage to take two
The keeper is standing up to the stumps with 1 needed off 2. All the fielders are inside the circle. Silly mid-off and silly mid-on in place. Plenty of close in fielders

Sam Curran to Jack Edwards, FOUR, and despite a jam-packed field inside the circle, Jack Edwards finds the gap. A low full toss outside off, Jack Edwards waits for it to dip in front of him, opens the bat face, and slices it through point for a boundary to seal the fate of the match. Jack Edwards is delighted as he's done the job for the Aussies. They win by 3 wickets and take a 1-0 lead in the series

Nikhil Chaudhary | Player of the Match(1/2): [On his first appearance for Australia on home soil at the MCG] It's always good to play for Australia. I had my first series in Bangladesh, which was good. We won that 3-0, but always wanted to play at home in Australia, and then nothing better than playing at MCG and winning that game. [On his bowling performance] Joel (Davies) started pretty good in the first over and then gave me the idea of actually the length and the line, and then I was just trying to hit the wickets at the start and obviously got that big wicket of Harry, which was a pretty good start. My main goal was to just keep hitting the wickets and bowl that five, six metre length.

Nikhil Chaudhary (2/2): [On Lachlan Shaw's catch] That was elite effort, that one. Obviously after a couple of drops, it's good to get back on the field with some great catches. [Batting under pressure and handling the verbal exchanges] You always obviously know it's a big game against England, so there's going to be a few chirp, and then you just have to stay stable and just keep playing your game, and hopefully I did that good at the crease and won the game for the team, which was great. [Born in Delhi, could you have ever imagined that you'd be Man of the Match for Australia at the MCG one day?] No, man, never imagined that. And my parents came over from India last night, so it's nothing better than getting a Man of the Match against them and it's their first game watching me play as well.

Mitchell Marsh (1/2): [On the entertaining game and its importance for Australian cricket] Yeah, thanks mate. No doubt Australia, pretty crazy 12 days. But I mean right there’s the future of our Australian cricket side with all those young guys in it. And yeah hopefully we can get back to enjoying that. [On the positive signs from the debutants and young players, including Joel Davies] Yeah, it was great. They’re a great bunch. We haven’t obviously spent a lot of time together. But I could tell they were all really excited. There was a few nerves in and around the group. I want them to not care about making mistakes and enjoy this environment and hopefully a win like that gives them a lot of confidence that they all certainly belong. It was great. [On whether Joel Davies was always going to open the bowling] Yes, well since yesterday.

Marsh (2/2): [On the dropped catches and the team’s fielding performance] Yeah, I was a little bit worried there. When you drop the best batsman in the world a couple of times, most of the time you don’t really deserve to win. But I thought outside of obviously a few tough chances, I thought the energy and the speed and I don’t know what it looked like, but it felt great to watch. And they’re all good kids, as I said before. That’s the future. We are 1-0 into this series. I know that, but it’s really positive signs. No doubt about it.

Australia drew first blood in the ODI series, but England responded strongly to claim the series 2-1. The Aussies have made a similar start to the T20I leg, taking a 1-0 lead. However, England have already shown their ability to bounce back. Can they repeat their ODI turnaround? We'll have to wait and see how things unfold over the next few days. For now, Australia have plenty of positives to take away from this contest; Nikhil Chaudhary's all-round brilliance, Sam Harper's explosive debut cameo and Jack Edwards' composure under pressure to finish the job.
